title: Research roundup: 6 cool science stories we almost missed
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: It’s a regrettable reality that there is never enough time to cover all the interesting scientific stories we come across. So every month, we highlight a handful of the best stories that nearly slipped through the cracks. September’s list includes a tantalizing hint of the elusive dark matter at the LUX-ZEPLIN detector; entangled Z bosons at the Large Hadron Collider; possible use of psychoactive substances in the Late Pleistocene; and an intriguing technical description of a telescope attributed to Galileo. A hint of dark matter? Physicists believe dark matter makes up roughly 85 percent of matter in our universe, with the strongest (but not only) candidate being so-called weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs). But directly detecting WIMPs, or other alternative hypothetical dark matter particles, has eluded physicists for decades. We might have our first glimpse, however, courtesy of the LUX-ZEPLIN detector buried deep in a gold mine in South Dakota. Those potentially exciting results were presented in a scientific talk at the 2026 TeV Particle Astrophysics conference in Japan, with a preprint available on the arXiv. (It has been submitted to Physical Review Letters for peer review.) The announcement came with strong caveats: the signal is just a hint, well below the threshold needed to confirm discovery, and might just be a statistical fluke. Anyone who regularly follows dark matter news knows that past tantalizing anomalies evaporated as more data came in. title: How I kept cool with NYC's free battery program for window AC units
author: Jeremy Hsu
body: My family has spent four summers participating in demand response programs whereby utility companies pay customers to reduce energy use on the hottest summer days. Most summers have involved carefully precooling our New York City apartment before switching off the air conditioners and sweating it out during the designated demand response periods. But this year, we kept our window air conditioners running throughout a heat dome event that drove daytime temperatures into the triple digits and made the nights oppressively hot. The difference was that we powered the air conditioners through two household batteries tucked away unobtrusively in the corners of our living room and bedroom. We were among about 1,000 New York City households that took part in a free and growing program offered by the local startup Every Electric. The company’s proposition is simple: Get one or more batteries delivered to your home, plug the batteries into a standard wall electrical outlet, and then plug your window air conditioners into the batteries. Households can keep running air conditioners as usual during peak demand periods while also earning money through the local demand response program with the utility company Con Edison. title: What is the SCP Foundation? Inside the internet horror universe headed to Hollywood.
body: For nearly two decades, writers on the internet have been adding to the SCP Foundation , a fictional world where a secret organization keeps supernatural creatures, strange objects, and unexplained phenomena hidden from the public. Their stories fill an online wiki, often taking the form of classified files detailing what each discovery does and how to keep it contained. Now, that world is heading to theaters. Neon has announced an SCP Foundation anthology movie for 2027, bringing multiple stories together in one film with a focus on emerging filmmakers. It joins the separately announced A24-backed V/H/S: SCP , an expansion of the V/H/S horror franchise being produced with Spooky Pictures and Image Nation Studios. Both films are targeting theatrical releases in 2027, so two different adaptations are in the works. If "SCP Foundation" means absolutely nothing to you, don't worry. You don't need to have spent years reading fictional incident reports to catch up. Here's everything you need to know about the collaborative writing project, the universe its contributors have created, and why Hollywood's interest has sparked debate. What is the SCP Foundation? Credit: Screenshot/SCP Foundation Wiki The name refers to both the fictional secret organization and the real collaborative writing project built around it. Within the stories, the Foundation locates, studies, and contains "anomalies": creatures, objects, places, or phenomena that defy the rules of reality. Its mission is to keep those anomalies hidden from the public and protect humanity, while also protecting the anomalies

title: YouTube Shorts is cracking down on clipping. Here’s what that means for creators.
body: If you spend time scrolling YouTube Shorts , you ve probably seen plenty of podcast excerpts, livestream highlights, and interview clips uploaded by someone other than the original creator. Taking moments from podcasts, interviews, livestreams, or other videos and repackaging them as short-form content is called "clipping," but now, YouTube wants those accounts to bring more to the table. According to an Oct. 2 announcement , YouTube is updating its Shorts recommendation systems to "improve the Shorts experience for everyone." The update encourages creators to upload "original commentary, unique edits, or storytelling." Want to learn more about getting the best out of your tech? Sign up for Mashable's Top Stories and Deals newsletters today. The change will work to further prioritize original content and reduce the reach of videos reposted from other creators without meaningful additions. But it could also complicate life for the wider clipping ecosystem, which many streamers and podcasters depend on to reach audiences. The platform also cautions against relying on "minor technical edits" or "template-based changes" simply to alter a video. The question, then, is what you re adding . Using a podcast excerpt to develop an argument or explain a topic is different from republishing that excerpt with a few cosmetic changes. Clipping has developed into a robust marketing business, with creators and brands paying accounts and fans to distribute short excerpts of their content . title: Grindr acquires HIV prevention med provider Freddie
body: Gay hookup app Grindr will acquire the telehealth provider Freddie , which provides PrEP medication to prevent HIV, the Wall Street Journal reported. The $250 million deal, in cash and stock, is the app's first major acquisition and represents an expansion beyond dating. The plan is to offer PrEP at little to no cost through Grindr's platform, Grindr CEO George Arison told the Wall Street Journal . SEE ALSO: The gay slang to know for your next vacation, according to Grindr The purchase is the "logical next step," Arison continued, "where we can deeply integrate the Grindr product experience with getting a medication that is lifesaving, and that a lot more people should be on than are on today." Freddie will be merged with Woodwork, the telehealth company Grindr launched last year, into a single Grindr Health experience, the Wall Street Journal reported. "Grindr Health is going to be an area of the business that we're going to focus a lot more on, in addition to our normal subscriptions and advertising," Arison said. Grindr agreed to pay 26 million to settle a lawsuit over allegations that it shared users' HIV statuses.

title: Meta’s Muse AI passes 5 million downloads, breaking records
body: Meta has a hit on its hands: its Muse AI assistant has proven extremely popular. Less than a month after Meta released Muse , the AI assistant has already surpassed 5 million downloads. Meta's Muse app reached this milestone on Wednesday, according to mobile data firm Sensor Tower. Muse hit 5 million downloads in just 3 weeks, even faster than long-established AI apps like OpenAI's ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude, and Elon Musk's Grok. ChatGPT took 56 days to reach 5 million downloads; Claude hit the mark at 103 days; and Grok needed 492 days to reach the milestone. The Muse app currently sits in the #1 position, topping both Apple's App Store and Google's Play app charts. SEE ALSO: 10 ways to use Meta's Muse AI app, from flight credits to outfit ideas According to Sensor Tower, while Muse has record downloads for an AI app, it's not breaking any general app records. Streaming services like Disney+ and HBO Max, games like Candy Crush , Pok mon Go , and Fortnite , and even Meta's own social media platform Threads all reached more than 5 million downloads within the same amount of time. Meta has gone all-in when it comes to promoting Muse. While the company appears to have succeeded so far, it hasn't been without controversy. There have been questions about how Meta, a company with a well-documented history of privacy failures , will handle user data with Muse . body: Tesla sold 486,532 electric vehicles during the third quarter of 2026. That’s a 2.1 percent decrease on the same quarter in 2025, when the company found homes for 497,099 EVs, and one might think that would be bad news for a company valued on the premise of near-constant growth. But Tesla stock is up this morning; the year-over-year numbers might look bad, but the company still exceeded analysts’ expectations of 456,600 cars, which would have been a larger 8 percent year-on-year decline Total production at Tesla actually increased year over year; it built 464,391 vehicles—a 3.7 percent increase—457,387 of which were Models 3 and Y (a 4.9 percent increase year over year). The remaining 7,004 were other models, mostly Cybertrucks, with presumably some Semis and Cybercabs, as the Models S and X are now retired; this category saw a 39.8 percent decrease year over year. title: Brooke Eby shared her life with ALS online, but her account was more than a diary
body: Editor's note (Oct. 2, 2026): Brooke Eby died at age 37 following her diagnosis with ALS, the ALS Network announced on Oct. 1. Eby, who posted under the name LimpBroozkit, began documenting her experience with the terminal neurodegenerative disease on TikTok in 2022, using humor and candor to educate hundreds of thousands of followers about ALS and build community among people living with the disease. "Levity is my superpower," Eby told Today in 2023, an ethos that defined much of her content even as her condition progressed. She later founded ALStogether , a nonprofit connecting people diagnosed with ALS with resources, experts, caregivers, and one another. In a 2025 essay for People , Eby reflected on the lasting purpose of documenting her illness online: "My TikTok presence will live on after I die. I hope it serves as a visual diary for anyone who gets diagnosed and needs a guide." Brooke Eby has built a deeply engaged following by documenting her life with ALS with humor, honesty, and a distinct point of view. Based in the Washington, DC area, Eby shares updates about her diagnosis and daily life with a tone that balances levity with reality. Across TikTok and Instagram , she's amassed hundreds of thousands of followers, drawn to her willingness to speak openly about disability, healthcare, and identity. Her posts often mix candid reflections with humor, creating a space that feels both personal and communal. title: When is the next Prime Day? Heres when to shop Amazons fall sale.
body: Amazon loves to keep us on our toes. We've been covering Prime Day for years, and even though the dates vary slightly, we expect Prime Day to fall in July. But this year, the retailer held its flagship sale in June, much to our surprise. This fall, however, things are back on schedule. Amazon's biggest sale of the year may be over, but there's another one upon us. We're here to lay out all the details you need to know because, surprise the early deals have started . When is the next Prime Day? While it may seem like Amazon holds sales every other month, Prime Day technically only happens once a year, in the summer. However, Amazon hosts a fall Prime event called Prime Big Deal Days, and it's coming up quickly. For all intents and purposes, it's colloquially known as October Prime Day. The official sale runs for 48 hours on Oct. 6 and Oct. 7 in 2026 , but you can expect deals in the days leading up to and following those dates. Amazon has also held a week-long shopping event in the spring, dubbed Amazon's Big Spring Sale, for the past three years. The deals aren't quite at the level of Prime Day, but it is considered Amazon's first major savings event of the year. After the October sale, it's the next time you'll hear the term "Prime Day" floating around. Are Prime Day deals worth it? Prime Day is notoriously full of great deals. Besides Black Friday, it's probably the best time of year to buy Amazon devices, Apple products, robot vacuums, everyday essentials, smartwatches, headphones, and more. The most recent version of the Shield streaming box debuted in 2019, running Android TV with AI upscaling and hardware decoding for almost any type of media. title: The Pocket Advance nearly perfects my favorite Nintendo handheld
body: Although I count the original Game Boy as one of my first tech obsessions, I still consider Nintendo’s Game Boy Advance to be my favorite console of all time thanks to its more comfortable horizontal design (for my big hands) and its expansive catalog of excellent 32-bit and 16-bit games. Ayaneo isn’t the first company to attempt to modernize the GBA, but its Konkr Pocket Advance does it best. The handheld strikes a near perfect balance between authentically re-creating the GBA’s design while updating its hardware with new controls, a much better screen, and the flexibility of Android at a price that feels like a bargain. As much as I still adore the GBA, I’ve eagerly embraced upgrades to the aging console over the years. First it was the clamshell GBA SP that finally delivered a frontlit screen I could actually see without a lamp over my shoulder, and later it was aftermarket upgrades like a backlit LCD display and a rechargeable battery that vastly improved Nintendo’s original hardware. Two years ago, I eagerly purchased Anbernic’s GBA-inspired RG34XX , but all of those have now been replaced by the Konkr Pocket Advance. It’s my first handheld from Ayaneo, and I’ve been pleasantly surprised to find the hardware feels on par with Nintendo’s. The Pocket Advance is an all-plastic affair but with a satisfying heft thanks to extra internal hardware including a cooling fan for its MediaTek Helio G90T processor and a 4,000mAh battery. Spears, and Fanatical: The Catfishing of Tegan and Sara . Now, she's tackling one of the most shocking reality TV series of the 2000s with The Swan: Behind The Mirror . Sitting down with Mashable Entertainment Editor Kristy Puchko in the Say More studio, Carr shared how she created a space for the swans to speak out, rewriting their narratives along the way. When she signed on to helm the project, it was important to her that empowerment be part of the story. Not only did she include every contestant who wanted to participate, but she also gathered the flock of swans for a reunion to celebrate their resilience and beauty (inside and out). Together, they also dig into some of the doc's most WTF reveals , including the nude photos that plastic surgeon Dr. Randal Haworth still has of the Season 2 contestants. Plus, Carr reflects on how she's grown a deep well of empathy that has been central to her work in documentary, whether talking to coerced reality TV stars or convicted killers. The Swan: Behind the Mirror is now streaming on Hulu.

title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on October 2, 2026
body: If you're heading outside tonight, don't forget to look up. The Moon is still very much visible in its current position in the lunar cycle, so, if the sky is clear, try and spot some craters or mares. What is today s Moon phase? As of Friday, Oct. 2, NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waning Gibbous phase, with 64% of its surface visible. With just your naked eye, tonight you can see the Mare Vaporum, the Oceanus Procellarum, and the Kepler Crater. If you have binoculars, you can also spot the Alps Mountains and the Alphonsus and Gassendi Craters. Finally, if you have access to a telescope, you'll see the Apollo 12 and 15 landing spots, plus the Rima Ariadaeus. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on October 25 or 26, depending on your timezone. What are Moon phases? The Moon takes around 29.5 days to orbit Earth, and as it moves through this cycle, we see different amounts of its sunlit side from here. That's what creates the Moon's different phases, from a thin crescent through to a half Moon and, eventually, the Full Moon. Once it reaches the Full Moon, the cycle starts over again. NASA explains that the phase we see depends on the Moon's position in relation to Earth and the Sun. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. title: TCL is right to question Samsung’s use of the term “Mini LED”
author: Scharon Harding
body: What makes a display a Mini LED display? It's a question that sounds like it should have a simple answer. But it's now at the center of a lawsuit between two of the biggest names in TVs, with TCL accusing its longtime competitor Samsung of falsely advertising budget LCD-LED TVs as Mini LED sets. TCL may have a point. Samsung's M-series TVs, which range from $300 for a 43-inch model to $2,300 for a 100-inch model, do raise some legitimate questions about what should qualify as Mini LED. More broadly, though, the dispute highlights a problem for shoppers: Without agreed-upon standards for what "Mini LED" actually means, manufacturers have plenty of room to define the technology for themselves. title: Tesla Model 3 gets more range, power, and a bigger display
body: Tesla 's Model 3 electric sedan has received a mild upgrade, though not every market got exactly the same features. In the U.S., the Model 3 now has a larger, 16-inch touchscreen (up form 15.4 inches), with a higher resolution. This goes for every variant, even the cheapest, Rear-Wheel Drive Model 3. For some variants, the changes aren't just cosmetic. The Model 3 Performance trim got 316 miles of range (up from 309) and 528 horsepower (up from 510); this variant also got the black headliner. And the Model 3 Premium AWD now accelerates quicker, with a 3.8 second 0-60mph time (down from 4.2 seconds). This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. The new features arrive shortly after Tesla announced a similar set of changes in China. There's one pretty big difference, though; in China, the Model 3 now also has V2L (vehicle to load) capability, meaning you can power other electric gadgets from the car's battery. In the U.S., this change isn't mentioned anywhere. SEE ALSO: Tesla Roadster launch was postponed by two weeks due to 'high winds' Another difference is the car's interior. In China, there's an option for a new, light gray interior; in the U.S. you can only choose between black, or black-and-white interior. The prices for all variants of the Model 3 in the U.S. haven't changed. The Rear-Wheel Drive Model 3 starts at $36,990, the Model 3 Premium starts at $42,490 (all-wheel drive option takes it to $47,490), and the Model 3 Performance, which is only available with the all-wheel drive, now starts at $54,990.

title: How violent was that planet crash? Astronomers check the dust.
body: Around some young stars, primitive planets smash into each other so hard they vaporize rock, leaving behind clouds of glassy bits in space . Softer glancing blows grind rock into something finer, like the green sand on some Hawaiian beaches. Astronomers found both types of crash debris while studying a sample of 21 young star systems. Each of these stars carries an unusually heavy load of warm dust in the same zone where Earth and the other rocky planets Mercury , Venus , and Mars orbit the sun . Astronomers call these "extreme debris disks," the detritus left over from smashups between rocky worlds about the size of our moon or Mars. These systems give scientists a window into the rough final stretch of building terrestrial planets, when scuffles between big bodies are common. By matching each system's dust to its age and behavior, researchers can learn when giant impacts happen, how violent they get, and which systems are still shuffling the positions of their planets. Our own solar system may have gone through this stage. Scientists think one of those collisions, involving a Mars-size world dubbed Theia , created the moon after slamming into early Earth. "How rocky planets formed and giant planets evolved are part of the broader story of the solar system s formation," said Kate Su, first author of the study, in a statement . "Our work on extreme debris disks helps us bring together the big picture." title: War stars Dominic West and Sienna Miller on episode 1s red carpet gone wrong
body: If the divorce at the center of War is, as its title suggests, an all-out war, then the end of the show's first episode is one hell of an opening shot. SEE ALSO: Yes, 'War's shocking episode 1 ending was inspired by Olivia Wilde's custody serving Throughout the episode, actor Carla Duval (Sienna Miller) plots to serve her husband, tech mogul Morgan Henderson (Dominic West), with divorce papers. Little does she know, he's caught wind of her intentions and is planning a quick counter. Carla's legal firm, Taylor Byrne , decides to serve Morgan via email after the premiere of her latest film. However, Morgan's firm, Cathcarts Sons, has something far more brutal in mind: serving Carla while she walks the red carpet at her premiere. It's a jaw-dropping moment, one that nods to how Jason Sudeikis' legal team served Olivia Wilde custody papers at CinemaCon . "I was so excited to shoot that scene because of the level of hiding that she would have to do," Miller told Mashable in a junket interview. "It felt like acrobatics, to some degree. What a nightmare to be in that position, with everybody looking at you and having to hide how wounded you are." West added: "It's delicious to play one thing when the audience knows something else is going on, and they're in on the secret. That's really fun to play, smiling while you're twisting a knife." West and Miller dive deep into the scene in the interview above, along with series creator George Kay and director Ben Taylor. New episodes of War premiere Thursdays at 9 p.m. ET on HBO and HBO Max.

title: Archie Renaux breaks down Wars game-changing mole twist
body: All's fair in love and War , including espionage. SEE ALSO: Yes, 'War's shocking episode 1 ending was inspired by Olivia Wilde's custody serving HBO and Sky's legal drama introduces ambitious lawyer Johnny Warren (Archie Renaux). He's just moved back to London after working at a Manhattan law firm, and he's on the hunt for a job in family law. However, as the first episode goes on, that job seems increasingly elusive. The firms he's interviewing at aren't impressed by his slick confidence or his time in New York. According to his references, his time there was far less successful than he claims it was. Still, by the episode's end, Johnny somehow winds up with a prime job at law firm Taylor Byrne, helping represent actor Carla Duval (Sienna Miller) in her divorce from tech mogul Morgan Henderson (Dominic West). Unfortunately for him, he didn't land the position on merit alone. His hiring was actually orchestrated by Morgan's law firm, Cathcarts Sons . Knowing Johnny would be interviewing with Taylor Byrne, Cathcarts offered him a job not to work directly for them, but to be a spy within Taylor Byrne's team. To make sure Johnny landed the job, Cathcarts' partner St. John Smallwood (Pip Torrens) called a friend at Johnny's old law firm and asked them to give Taylor Byrne a glowing recommendation. That recommendation plus Johnny's reveal he was entertaining an offer from Cathcarts were all law partners Nicholas Taylor (James McArdle) and Serena Byrne (Phoebe Fox) needed to bring him onboard. Morgan serving Carla in public at an important career event immediately recalls how Jason Sudeikis' legal team served his ex-partner Olivia Wilde with custody papers in 2022. A process server served Wilde while she was onstage at CinemaCon, promoting her second feature film, Don't Worry Darling . In a 2026 appearance on the Call Her Daddy podcast, Wilde described the experience as "one of the most fucked-up things that I went through" and "incredibly traumatizing." In 2022, sources told Variety that Sudeikis "had no prior knowledge of the time or place that the envelope would have been delivered." title: Who are we expecting to save us from AI?
body: On Wednesday, the New York Times reported that Meta has been treating its AI data centers as experimental facilities to claim billions of dollars in federal research tax credits, a strategy the company's own accountants reportedly flagged as legally risky. The savings reportedly grew from $700 million in 2023 to $3.9 billion in 2025. How can a company worth $1.8 trillion be worried about saving $3.9 billion? Well, because the priorities of any publicly traded company are profits, then stock price, then market cap, then penny-pinching, and then the cycle repeats. The Meta story underscores something simple: the people building the most powerful technology on Earth will push the rules when money is on the line. Yet they now ask us to trust them on safety, to believe they are putting financial gain aside to do the right thing. Give me a break. SEE ALSO: AI leaders say they want safety, but on whose terms? Everyone is spinning over whether AI chatbots could go rogue. Will it happen? Can it be stopped? Is the threat real, or a hoax? Here's a better question: who do we trust to tell us the truth, and to act when it matters? The canaries in the coal mine are chirping, and there's more than one bird. OpenAI announced it is shelving its newest model because it didn't quite meet the bar on safety. Anthropic's CEO has warned that, within a year , AI could be capable of directing a swarm of agents that takes over the internet. title: Venus' mysterious haze is actually cosmic dust
author: Elizabeth Rayne
body: Venus is shrouded in a veil of mystery. The yellowish “lower haze” at the bottom of its atmosphere was discovered by the Venera and Pioneer Venus probes in the 1970s. These spacecraft were some of the first to successfully send images of the planet back to Earth, but the haze they saw went unexplained for decades. Now the mystery Venus was keeping has been unveiled. What nobody knew then was that the haze is an accumulation of particles from meteorites. “Shooting stars” that burn up in the atmosphere leave behind cosmic dust particles, and after sulfuric acid interacts with these particles, it leaves behind a haze. Planetary scientist Hiroki Karyu and his research team at Tohoku University in Sendai City, Japan, finally figured out how the haze formed using a microphysical model. This type of model involves microphysics —the micro-scale processes that create clouds and precipitation on Earth and other bodies. “The continuous influx of cosmic dust is sufficient to sustain this lower haze layer with the particle size distribution observed by the entry probes,” Karyu said in a study published in Nature Astronomy. “These haze particles of cosmic origin act as efficient condensation nuclei, promoting cloud formation in the main cloud deck even far from their initial source.” Read full article Comments

title: Hacks of 2 federal agencies in a month have spilled a bonanza of sensitive data
author: Dan Goodin
body: The Pentagon is informing more than 2 million current and former military members that their personnel records storing sensitive personal information were stolen over a monthslong compromise of one of its networks. The breach is the second one in recent months to expose sensitive government information. The records, according to one notification letter posted to Reddit, included Social Security numbers, names, addresses, sex, race, and occupational specialty. This last category could be particularly valuable to foreign adversaries because it could help their intelligence agencies in identifying high-value military personnel. Starting last October, hackers gained access to a system operated by the Defense Manpower Data Center , which collates Department of Defense personnel records. The Pentagon says that the breach compromised the records of 2.8 million living individuals. A potential boon The incident is the second time a major network breach in recent months has exposed sensitive US government personnel records that criminal groups or foreign adversaries could use. Last month, the ransomware group ShinyHunters claimed it hacked into FBI systems and stole records of thousands of the agency’s current or former employees. Reuters reported the job titles in the records included ones related to investigating China or Russia. Read full article Comments

title: Judge dismisses Chegg and Penske antitrust lawsuits targeting Google AI search
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: In a setback for publishers worried about the effects of AI search, a US federal judge has dismissed lawsuits filed by Chegg and Penske Media against Google. The companies accused Google of antitrust violations in products like AI overviews, which have led to decreasing traffic at numerous sites. However, US District Judge Amit Mehta has ruled that Google's conduct is not illegal under antitrust law. The lawsuits were filed in 2025 , and Google requested a dismissal earlier this year. Chegg, an education and learning platform, claimed in its lawsuit that Google illegally scraped its educational content. This allowed Gemini models to essentially recreate that content and reduce the site's traffic. Penske, which owns publications like Rolling Stone and Variety, filed a similar case that alleged lost traffic . Specifically, the publisher claimed it was unfair that sites indexed for organic search would also have their content harvested for AI answers, with no way to opt out. These arguments did not sway the judge, who noted that Google's implicit agreement with websites is not legally relevant. "Plaintiffs have pleaded only that they have an ‘expectation’ that Google will send them search ​traffic if they make their content available for free," wrote Mehta. "But an expectation is not an agreement. It is simply how a general search engine works." Read full article Comments

title: I am Jane Doe: The internet rallies to protect a Cornell students identity
body: Scroll through social media, and you'll likely see the same sentence repeated over and over: "I am Jane Doe." From comedians to authors to creators to everyday users, people are lending their names to a movement aimed at protecting the identity of the former Cornell University student who alleges that seven Chi Phi fraternity members sexually assaulted her in 2024. Why? The movement gained momentum after political commentator Michael Tracey publicly solicited information identifying the woman, who filed her civil lawsuit under a pseudonym. "Let's see if anyone has the 'balls' to name this Jane Doe so we can all evaluate her veracity," he wrote Sept. 28. He followed up that he would be "happy to publish her name and identifying information" and that "this is 100% permitted under the First Amendment." This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. That prospect sparked an immediate response from people who wanted her identity kept private. Doxxing generally refers to exposing someone s personal information online without their permission. In this case, supporters are pushing back against the idea that bringing allegations into public view should also mean opening the woman s personal life to scrutiny. SEE ALSO: Instagram put a warning on Florence Pugh's 'Cornell 7' post. Why? Their answer has been to make themselves part of the search. On Threads, participants are posting "I am Jane Doe," sometimes pairing the declaration with their own names and inviting others to do the same. "I guess this is a thing now," Tracey wrote Sept. 30 about the trend

title: Can good design stop content creators from having sex in robotaxis?
author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
body: Humans can be a frisky bunch, and it wasn’t very long after Tesla Autopilot started letting drivers go hands-free before people decided to post footage of themselves having sex from the driver’s seat. Recently, The San Francisco Standard interviewed multiple people who claimed to have had sex in robotaxis belonging to General Motors’ now-defunct Cruise. “There’s no one to tell you, 'You can’t do that.' It gets to the point where you’re more and more and more comfortable, and if you’re with someone, like a more serious partner, it can escalate to other activities,” one man told SF Standard. “The interiors of vehicles has been sexualized and appropriated for sex since forever in popular culture. You can see it in movies, you can see it in lyrics, you can see it in photography,” said Alexandros Rouchitsas, a human factors/UX researcher and one of the organizers of a recent workshop, “ Love in Traffic ,” that brought researchers from academia and industry together in late September in Sweden to consider how design can help the problem. A growing problem? One difference between a robotaxi and a human-driven ride is the removal of the social obligation to interact with a human driver. There’s no need to make small talk, and you won’t have to listen to someone’s terrible opinion, which can lead to riders assuming far more privacy than the cameras and ridership terms and conditions provide. That's a lesson that a pair of teens who hired a Waymo, spent their ride getting drunk, and shot gel beads out the windows learned the hard way this summer. Read full article Comments

title: FedExs new order for EV trucks will save them hundreds of millions in fuel costs
body: With a plan to fully electrify its fleet by 2040, FedEx recently took a big step toward that goal by purchasing 2,000 EVs that will enter service in the U.S. and Canada by the end of 2027. The Tennessee-based package carrier is buying the vehicles from California startup Harbinger for over $200 million , according to InsideEVs. If the report s numbers are right, it s a good investment; the trucks are anticipated to save FedEx $40 miillion in fuel costs each year and, with each EV truck engineered to last 20 years, that s $800 million in savings. SEE ALSO: How California's high-speed rail is already helping the planet Over the same period, the new trucks aim to prevent 1.7 million tons of carbon dioxide from entering the atmosphere. The medium-duty EV trucks can travel between 140 and 210 miles on a full charge; Harbinger officials say a 20-to-80 percent charge takes less than an hour on a fast charger. FedEx has about 175,000 vehicles on the road , according to its own estimates. The company s climate goals include exclusively purchasing electric trucks by 2030. By 2040, the company is committed to having all its pickup and delivery vehicles be zero-tailpipe emission models, including contracted transportation.

title: iPhone 18 Pro and Max speaker popping noises reported by Redditors
body: Is there an audio or speaker problem with the new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max ? On Reddit and Apple forums , some users have been complaining about a crackling or "popping noise" coming from their new iPhones' speakers. Some of the users think the issue stems from the earpiece speaker, and Mashable found complaints about the problem with both the Pro and Pro Max models. We also want to note that multiple Mashable reporters have a new iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max device ( read our full review ), and none have experienced any audio popping issues. However, the potential issue has been reported in multiple places. Mashable reached out to Apple to ask about a possible speaker issue and will update this piece if we receive a response. One Redditor described the issue as sounding as "if someone is pulling out an aux cord and you hear a brief click pop noise." The user said the clicking noise occurred during numerous activities, from playing music to switching apps to receiving notifications. One user reported that an Apple Store employee told them that this was most likely a software issue that would be fixed with an update. However, the latest iOS 27.0.1 update , which was released earlier this week, did not fix the audio problem for some of the users who reported experiencing the problem, according to posts on Reddit. title: With most information hidden, the game Stratego had stumped AI—until now
author: Jacek Krywko
body: Deep Blue took down Garry Kasparov at chess in 1997, AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol at Go in 2016, and poker bots have been beating professionals for years. But one classic game called Stratego held out. Even DeepMind, with its exceptional budget, couldn't build a machine that reliably beat the best human players. Now, a team of researchers from Carnegie Mellon, MIT, New York University, and Stanford University has done it. Their AI, called Ataraxos, beat Pim Niemeijer, arguably the best Stratego player of all time, 15 games to one, with four draws. And it took just 16 GPUs and a few thousand dollars to train it. Hidden armies In Stratego , each player gets 40 pieces representing military ranks, from a marshal down to a spy, plus bombs and a flag. You win by capturing the opponent's flag. Your opponent knows where your pieces are, but not what they are. Identities are revealed only when two pieces collide in battle—the weaker one is removed, and the identity of the winner is revealed. That makes Stratego an imperfect-information game, just like poker, which computers cracked years ago. “There's something super distinctive about Stratego , which is that it is a massive amount of hidden information that unfolds over a very long time scale,” said Eugene Vinitsky, a researcher at NYU and co-author of the study. title: Reddit will block Old Reddit for users who don’t use it for six months
body: If you're a Reddit user who prefers the old Reddit platform, colloquially referred to as "Old Reddit," over the newly designed one, then you're going to want to pay attention to this. According to Reddit , the company will start blocking Old Reddit for Redditors that haven't used Old Reddit in the previous six months. Reddit previously limited Old Reddit only to users who are logged into their account. "In the next few months, we'll further limit access for logged-in users to only those who have used Old Reddit in the last six months (which covers the vast majority of all Old Reddit users)," Reddit posted in r/modnews. The Reddit employee who posted this news added that this change will not apply to logged-in platform mods. They can continue to use Old Reddit without any usage requirements. This latest move appears to point to the company eventually moving away from the old version of the platform, although Reddit has not yet committed to that publicly, at least. "We re still working on the future of Old Reddit," the employee posted alongside the usage announcement. These changes over at Reddit, including the recently announced shutdown of RSS feeds and its public API, have been attributed to the rise of AI bots, according to the company. Sure, something interesting might eventually happen, but no one outside of a few Canadian space geeks was paying much attention. But then the Trump Administration started threatening and instituting tariffs. There was talk of making Canada the 51st state. And pretty much every Canadian I know began telling me how enraged they were at their neighbors to the south. It's hard to blame them. This has led the Canadian government to reassess all manner of areas where it had previously been happy to rely largely on the US government and American companies for goods and services. This included sovereign access to space. So this spring, the government announced the first awards to three companies—NordSpace, Reaction Dynamics, and Canada Rocket Company—to support work on rockets with "light lift" capability. title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on October 1, 2026
body: Wondering what the Moon will look like tonight? Its shape and brightness change throughout the month, so there's always something slightly different to see on its surface. Here's the lunar phase for tonight, plus what you might be able to see. What is today s Moon phase? As of Thursday, Oct. 1, NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waning Gibbous phase, with 75% of its surface visible. Without any visual aids, tonight you can see the Copernicus Crater, Oceanus Procellarum, and the Kepler Crater. If you have binoculars, you can also spot the Clavius, Alphonsus, Gassendi Craters. Finally, if you have access to a telescope, you'll see the Apollo 11 and 15 landing spots, plus the Descartes Highlands. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on October 25 or 26, depending on your timezone. What are Moon phases? The Moon takes around 29.5 days to orbit Earth, and as it moves through this cycle, we see different amounts of its sunlit side from here. That's what creates the Moon's different phases, from a thin crescent through to a half Moon and, eventually, the Full Moon. Once it reaches the Full Moon, the cycle starts over again. NASA explains that the phase we see depends on the Moon's position in relation to Earth and the Sun. The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). title: Inside our months-long investigation into Kevin O’Leary’s Utah data center debacle
body: Today I’m talking with Josh Dzieza, a longtime features writer here at The Verge , about Kevin O’Leary’s plans to build a massive data center in Utah . The idea was to build the world’s biggest data center — a 40,000-acre AI campus with nine gigawatts of power, or more than double the average power usage of the entire state of Utah. The project is technically called Stratos, but it’s more prominently known as Wonder Valley, a reference to O’Leary’s nickname on Shark Tank . Josh has spent months reporting on this project, and it’s fair to say Wonder Valley has completely upended Utah politics. What Josh found throughout the course of his reporting was that the way this data center came together — how it was planned, how it was announced and approved, and how local residents were kept in the dark — ultimately created a political firestorm so severe it stopped Stratos in its tracks. Now, the details of what happened with Wonder Valley are obviously fascinating. But the story is also a larger look at the AI industry’s infrastructure boom, the bipartisan backlash to that buildout, and how the tech industry is running into the one obstacle it can’t seem to spend its way out of: local democracy. It already has two film adaptations, a sequel, a miniseries adaptation, and even a Royal Shakespeare Company musical (yes, really). How can you possibly take a tale that's such a big part of popular culture and do something new with it? Well, Mike Flanagan has had a good go. title: PS5 emulation is suddenly making big strides on PC
author: Kyle Orland
body: For a long time, PC gamers could access many PlayStation 5 games only if the publisher invested in a bespoke port (something Sony has recently said it will be scaling back ). Now, though, rapid advancements in PS5 emulators and other tools are making recent PlayStation titles increasingly playable on generic PCs. SharpEmu was the first of these emulators, advancing from a "very early alpha stage" in May to a current state that can "load the eboot.bin of real games, execute native CPU instructions, and partially handle GPU-related functionality." The most recent release boasts 10 tested games that reach a "playable" state , including six that developer CursedIfElse says are "fully playable at 60 fps." That includes simple 2D games like Tetris Forever but also 3D titles like Astro Bot and the PS5 Demon's Souls remaster running at playable frame rates. "SharpEmu has prioritized hardware accuracy from the very beginning, and we’re finally starting to see that investment pay off," CursedIfElse wrote on social media this week . "It was built completely from scratch, and this is how far we’ve come." Read full article Comments

title: NASA squeezed Treasury, vibe coded, and broke the mold in bid to save Swift
author: Stephen Clark
body: An attempt to save NASA's $500 million Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory from dropping out of orbit fell short, but the behind-the-scenes machinations required just to make a rescue possible deserve recognition, government and commercial space officials said in a recounting of the mission. The rescue mission was developed by Katalyst Space Technologies, working under a $30 million contract awarded by NASA last September. NASA gave Katalyst nine months to build and launch a satellite to capture Swift flying some 200 miles above the Earth and boost it into a higher orbit. Katalyst's rescue spacecraft, known as Link, successfully launched July 3 and completed some of its initial checkouts before a malfunction caused it to spin out of control a few weeks later. NASA announced in August that Link would not be able to reach Swift as intended, and the rescue mission was aborted. Read full article Comments

It is so powerful, Google claims, that it's already "fundamentally changing" how Google works and builds its products internally. In a blog post, the company offers some details as to what that means. In one example, a team of Argon agents analyzed memory usage in Google's data centers and optimized it, freeing over 300 TiB (tebibytes; one TiB is roughly 1.1 terabytes) of memory. We get it, Argon is the new king of the hill...until the next one comes along. Credit: Google According to Google's data, Gemini 4 Argon outperforms OpenAI GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, and Claude Opus 5.5 on most benchmarks. In the post, Google highlighted that it trained Argon to be particularly capable in cybersecurity defense and that it can "autonomously find, validate, and patch critical software vulnerabilities." Ever since the three county commissioners unanimously approved his data center the week before, O’Leary had observed a sudden increase in people mad at him online. The PlayStation maker is requiring that consumers prove they've put in time playing on a PlayStation before they can even enter for a chance to buy a console. title: Dinosaur-killing impact crater might have been teeming with life
author: Elizabeth Rayne
body: About 66 million years ago, the Chicxulub asteroid smashed into Earth, kicking up tsunamis and dropping hot debris that annihilated non-avian dinosaurs and many other species. But not everything it left in its wake was destructive. This space rock hit what is now the partially submerged Yucatan Peninsula, and at the bottom of the ocean, the impact generated enough heat to create a hydrothermal system that persisted for 8 million years and may have been a hotbed of life. When researchers drilled for samples in the impact zone in 2016, they studied the types of rock that had formed as a result of the asteroid strike. This gave more insight into what happened in the immediate and long-term aftermath of this cataclysmic event. The collision was intense enough to cause deformation far beneath the surface. Subterranean effects reached 35 km (almost 22 miles) down, and included the melting an immense amount of rock. Exposure to seawater made that rock porous. As hot water seeped into the pores, a hydrothermal system formed. The hot water gushing into an isolated region of the freezing depths could have attracted microorganisms and possibly other life forms that were otherwise struggling to survive. title: Reddit is ending RSS feeds — with no replacement. You can blame AI bots.
body: AI bots are making it harder to be a human who just wants to read Reddit . The company is shutting down its RSS feeds on Nov. 13, 2026, and ending public API access in March 2027. Announced on Wednesday, Sept. 30, in a channel for moderators (and reported by TechCrunch ), the changes are a response to automated scraping, but they will also affect people who use outside tools to follow conversations and manage Reddit communities. What s happening to Reddit s RSS feeds? RSS, short for Really Simple Syndication, lets you subscribe to website updates and read them in a feed reader. Think of it as bringing posts from different places into one inbox, without visiting each site individually. For Reddit users, that means following favorite subreddits or setting up moderation alerts. But the company says RSS has become a "common surface for large-scale scraping and automated abuse," and is pulling the plug. Reddit recommends that moderators move common alerts to Discord Relay , an app on its developer platform, Devvit . For everyone else, the options are less promising: "If you use RSS for feeds outside of a community you moderate, there is no replacement," the company wrote. That leaves some readers figuring out how to keep up. "That sucks because I use a Chrome extension called RSS Feed Reeder to be notified of every new post in my subs," wrote one user. "I don't know how I'll do that now on my desktop computer." Another commenter said their team uses an RSS feed to send Reddit status updates to its moderation Discord. title: A local network of implants uses your body as the wiring
author: Jacek Krywko
body: Most implants like pacemakers and insulin pumps work in isolation. To help them coordinate with each other, a team of Georgia Tech researchers built a networking system that sends signals through body tissue instead of antennas and radio waves. Radio problems Implants that communicate today mostly rely on radio protocols like Bluetooth Low Energy or near-field communication (NFC). Both are a poor fit for in-body data transfer, says Alex Abramson, a Georgia Tech engineer and co-author of the new study. The first problem is power. “If you want an implant to remain in an active state such that it can respond within milliseconds, it's very difficult to do that with the Bluetooth system,” Abramson said. According to the paper, Bluetooth components, when they’re activated, can cut an implant's battery life by up to 90 percent. Read full article Comments

title: Attackers have been exploiting critical Zimbra flaw to steal emails
author: Dan Goodin
body: Hackers have been exploiting a critical vulnerability in the Zimbra Collaboration Suite in an attempt to obtain email backups and authentication credentials of vulnerable organzations, Microsoft has warned . The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-73570, lets attackers remotely issue operating system commands without authentication. Zimbra maintainer Synacor issued a patch on July 20, but didn’t disclose the vulnerability for more than three weeks after that. The security-focused Shadowserver Foundation said last week that its scans found that 274 separate instances of the Zimbra Collaboration Suite had been compromised. The number of servers running the software has fluctuated from 19,000 in the week following the patch to about 12,000 in the weeks following that. Currently, Shadowserver is tracking about 10,000 instances. Look, ma, no authorization From July 28 to August 7, Microsoft said Wednesday, the company detected two distinct scanning tools probing the Internet for vulnerable endpoints. The attackers first validated their exploit worked by sending HTTP, requests and DNS, ICMP, and out-of-band identity checks to domains hosted on public services. The probes allowed the attackers to confirm the exploit successfully executed commands on vulnerable servers without actually compromising them. Eventually, the attackers began using their command injection capability to install malicious payloads. Microsoft wrote: Read full article Comments

title: Google announces Gemini 4 Argon AI model, but you can't use it yet
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: Google promised Gemini 3.5 Pro in June, but it spent the summer trotting out smaller Flash models . Now, Google is ready to take on the frontier again with Gemini 4 Argon . The company claims this new AI offers industry-leading performance in coding, knowledge work, and cybersecurity, but you aren't allowed to use it yet. While most of us will have to wait to test Gemini 4, Google says engineers inside the company are already using the new model extensively. Argon reportedly used "fleet-wide telemetry data" to help Google save 300 TiB of memory across its data centers. Meanwhile, Argon agents have been working to migrate C/C++ codebases to Rust across Google, including thousands of lines in the core re2 and libgav1 libraries and more than 800,000 lines in the Fuchsia OS Zircon kernel. Google has also come armed with a raft of benchmarks to back up its claims. On the software engineering DeepSWE v1.1 benchmark, Gemini 4 Argon hits 77.9 percent, which is higher than GPT-6 Astra, Fable 5.1, and Opus 5.5. Google promises similar power across a range of long-horizon tasks, pointing to Argon's industry-leading score in the economic analysis Vals Index test. Read full article Comments

While MAHA generally coalesces around things like healthy lifestyles and mistrust of drugmakers, Kennedy quickly turned to extolling the potential of artificial intelligence, surprising Vance, who said he was expecting to discuss "weight loss and acid, not AI." Kennedy boasted that the Trump administration is "making it easy for every American to use AI," which he claimed would free us from the "medical tyranny" of doctors and health experts. He suggested Americans should start using AI to get second opinions about medical recommendations, saying AI is "better informed than any doctor in the country." He also suggested that the technology would confirm his misinformation about vaccines and contrarian views on public health guidance. "We're never, ever again going to be able to be dominated by public officials who tell us trust the experts, because every American will be able to check their own medical advice," Kennedy said. Disney's ubiquity Canceling Disney+ was simple but threw a hefty wrench into my evening routine. I tend to end many weekdays laughing at comforting sitcom reruns and adult animation. title: Did Muse read private texts without permission? Meta says it couldn’t.
body: Meta's Muse is supposed to help with your digital life. But a dispute over its access to private messages raises a basic question about exactly how much users are letting it see. In a Sept. 19 column for Inc. , tech writer Jason Aten said he installed Muse on his iPhone and Mac and asked it to research his background and suggest ways it could help. Later, he said, the agent suggested a story idea based on a private text conversation with his podcast co-host, Stephen Robles, about the new iPhones. It also flagged a message from his editor about a deadline. "I never gave it permission to read my messages," Aten wrote. He said he remembered explicitly declining access to his messages, calendar, and other personal information during setup. So he asked how it knew what he was texting. Muse claimed the Mac app was passing along incoming notification banners. "It s the incoming notification stream only, not access to your texts," the agent told him, according to Aten. But Aten said his investigation suggested Muse had synced his local Messages database, reaching row 187,462. That isn t necessarily a count of individual messages, but his account suggests access beyond incoming notifications. He also said Muse's settings showed Full Disk Access was disabled. Screenshots of Jason Aten's conversation with Meta s Muse. Credit: Screenshot/Jason Aten Screenshots of Jason Aten questioning Meta's Muse about its access to his private messages. title: Lawsuit demands OpenAI halt unsafe development that caused Hugging Face hack
author: Jon Brodkin
body: OpenAI's hack of Hugging Face in July 2026 has spurred a lawsuit demanding that the company stop accessing third-party computer systems and halt AI development practices that can harm the public. The lawsuit was filed by Legal Advocates for Safe Science Technology (LASST), which said yesterday that the hack in which OpenAI "agents stole credentials, uploaded malicious files, and gained control over key parts of Hugging Face’s internal systems... is unquestionably illegal under California law." California’s Comprehensive Computer Data Access and Fraud Act (CDAFA) prohibits unauthorized access into computer systems, "and it doesn’t matter that a swarm of AI agents carried out this cyberattack. California law makes it clear that it is not a defense 'that the artificial intelligence autonomously caused the harm,'" the group said. The lawsuit , filed in San Francisco County Superior Court, said OpenAI also violated California's Unfair Competition Law (UCL). "OpenAI’s insistence on externalizing the harms of its unsafe decision-making is a fundamentally unfair business practice," the complaint said, adding that "such risk-taking for private gain at substantial public expense is immoral, unethical, oppressive, unscrupulous, and substantially injurious conduct." body: Executives from iconic publications like Esquire, Cosmopolitan, Vogue , and Vanity Fair are descending on Washington to lobby for another AI regulation bill , this time tackling the threat AI poses to their bottom lines and longevity. Introduced to the House in July, the bipartisan Stealth Bot Prohibition Act would prohibit the deployment of "stealth bots," or unidentified AI agents tasked with scraping and indexing a website's content, without disclosure. Should it pass, bot scrapers and their purposes would have to be clearly identified to website publishers or risk civil penalties under the Federal Trade Commission. Attorneys general would also be authorized to take action against AI scraping. SEE ALSO: Kids aren't learning to type anymore Backed by the trade nonprofit News/Media Alliance, the group is calling for federal regulation to level the playing field as AI dominates website traffic, search, and discoverability and puts many publishers at risk. "We are drowning in bot traffic that is hurting our ability to serve our readers, and existing technical tools simply aren t enough to protect our content from malicious actors that can disguise their identity," wrote News/Media Alliance president Danielle Coffey at the time of the bill's introduction. "We need transparency and accountability for bad actors, as well as enforcement mechanisms that require the most basic transparency disclosure." title: So what's happening with Russia's new, long-delayed crewed spacecraft?
author: Eric Berger
body: In what seems like an alternate universe in hindsight, Russia and the European Space Agency began discussing collaboration on next-generation crewed spacecraft two decades ago. Under the agreement , Europe would have provided a service module to power a crew capsule carrying up to six passengers. Europe ultimately decided not to pursue a crewed spacecraft project at the time, and Russia's state-backed space corporation, Roscosmos, chose to move ahead with a crewed spacecraft on its own. This project—always seemingly more of a Potemkin village than an effort encompassing real hardware—has gone under various guises over the years: PPTS (Perspektivnaya Pilotiruemaya Transportnaya Sistema / Prospective Piloted Transport System): The initial conceptual project name used in 2009 PTK NP (Pilotiruyemy Transportny Korabl Novogo Pokoleniya / New Generation Piloted Transport Ship): The official technical designation used until 2016 Federatsiya (Federation): The official name chosen following a public contest and announced in January 2016 Orel / Oryol (Eagle) : A new name adopted in September 2019 when Roscosmos was under the control of Dmitry Rogozin Actual hardware tests, maybe? Beyond the name changes and a flood of renderings, after nearly 20 years of work, then, is anything actually happening with the Eagle spacecraft? Read full article Comments

title: Google's early attempt to pay websites for AI answers is struggling
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: Google's shift to AI-powered search has upended the way the world's largest search engine generates web traffic, rankling large and small publishers alike. In recent months, the company has experimented with paying publishers when their content appears in AI answers, but a new report claims the payouts in this pilot program are miniscule. That has publishers in the program, as well as those watching from the sidelines, feeling skeptical. According to The Information , Google has admitted about 100 publishers to the AI contribution pilot. The pitch is that websites can get payments from Google when their content materially contributes to Gemini-powered search results like an AI Overview. Google has long resisted the idea of direct payments to publishers, arguing that websites get traffic in exchange for allowing Google bots to scrape their content for use in search and knowledge graph tools. In the age of AI, that relationship is breaking down, hence the AI pilot. So far, publishers aren't getting much for their trouble. The Information heard from several small and mid-sized publishers in the program that Google's AI payments are minuscule, equaling roughly one-tenth of one percent of their advertising revenue. These payments have been so disappointing that several larger publishers have reportedly declined to participate in the program. These publishers hope that by refusing to join the pilot, they can force Google to offer a more generous deal. Read full article Comments

title: Google figures out how to watermark AI-designed proteins
author: John Timmer
body: AI-based tools seem to be causing security threats on a nearly daily basis, in part because we've been slow to recognize potential threats. One area where we seem to be ahead of the game, however, is in biosecurity. As with most things biological, utility goes hand in hand with threats. We've developed increasingly sophisticated tools for designing proteins and seen some major successes, such as AI-designed enzymes that can digest plastics or block venom proteins . But these same tools could be used to make toxins or alter the behavior of viral proteins. And the software we use to identify DNA sequences that encode potentially threatening proteins doesn't pick out AI-designed proteins , since nobody has characterized them well enough to know that they're threats. Nearly a year after that risk was flagged, it still wasn't clear what anyone could do about it. Read full article Comments

title: The PS5 hacking scene just took a big leap forward
author: Kyle Orland
body: For a few years now , the PS5 hacking community has been chipping away at various exploits that let users fully jailbreak their locked-down console. For the most part, though, those exploits have only worked with years-old versions of the PS5's frequently updated firmware , making them less than useful for many everyday users. That changed Tuesday with the release of the new Relapse exploit , which works with any PS5 up to firmware version 13.6 (released in July). That means jailbreaking is now possible on any PS5 that was last updated before the mid-September release of firmware version 14.00.00 . The so-called Relapse exploit makes use of a long-known WebKit vulnerability in the PS5's hard-to-access web browser , escalating from there to gain write access to the PS5 kernel and install an ELF loader to streamline the running of arbitrary code. The new method is also a lot more efficient than previous PS5 jailbreak exploits, which could hang the system for 50 minutes per attempt . Read full article Comments

title: What butterfly wings have in common with barbershop poles
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: Old-fashioned striped barbershop poles turn in place on a vertical axis, but humans typically perceive the stripes moving upward rather than turning with the pole. It's a well-known visual illusion arising from processing biases in human vision. According to a new paper published in the journal Nature, a similar effect could explain how butterflies often evade predatory birds: Their flight patterns and wing patterns combine to make it hard for predators to accurately gauge speed and direction. "The stripes and spots on many butterflies’ wings interfere with the way visual systems try to guess the direction and speed of moving things, boosting false motion cues while hiding the butterfly's true heading," said co-author George Hancock of the University of Exeter in Cornwall. "The illusions interfere with the predator’s most basic visual targeting system and disrupt the final ‘ballistic attack’ in the tens of milliseconds when it commits to grabbing its prey, with no time to change course. As a result, birds and other predators will often simply miss." Butterfly wings have long fascinated scientists, ever since the first documentation of the growth of said wings back in 1938. By 2021, researchers at MIT had captured on video the unique structural growth of butterfly wings—continuously, as a butterfly develops inside its chrysalis—for the very first time. Butterfly wings are an example of structural color in nature: the bright iridescent colors don’t come from pigment molecules but from what physicists call photonic crystals . title: Verity review: Anne Hathaway gives top-notch psycho-biddy
body: Anne Hathaway deserves more credit for her capabilities as a camp queen. Yes, yes, she's popular and respected for her work in mainstream movies like The Devil Wears Prada 2 and masterful cinema like The Odyssey. But for my money, Hathaway's filmography is at its most exciting when she plunges into anti-heroine depths, playing women who aren't just messy, but menacing and even deadly. For your consideration, remember Colossal, where she played a drunkard who manifests a kaiju over Seoul, or Serenity, an under-sung psycho-sexual thriller where she sunk her pearly white teeth into the role of femme fatale. Look to Eileen , where she played a psychologist on a twisted mission, or NEON's scuttled Mother's Instinct, where she snarled as a picture-perfect mother destroyed by the death of her child. Even earlier this year, Hathaway offered a diva-level performance as a haunted pop star in Mother Mary , which is not to be overlooked. But unexpectedly, it's in the very mainstream adaptation of Colleen Hoover's best-selling novel Verity that Hathaway gives her wildest performance of 2026. (Yes, even considering the dinos-on-the-loose The End of Oak Street .) In Verity, Hathaway plays the title character, massively popular novelist Verity Crawford, who is known for her Noble Virtues series, each told from the point of view of a bloodthirsty villain. Tailored dresses and cashmere cardigans the color of fresh blood make Hathaway's pale skin look luminescent and hard like marble. title: Group chats have come to Tinder
body: Today, dating app Tinder launches a group chat feature called Group Hangouts in the U.S. It builds on the app's Double Date Mode to help form connections through friends and groups. With Group Hangouts, three or more people can add an IRL activity, like karaoke, and find other groups with shared interests to start chatting and matching. "Double Date proved something we suspected all along, young singles want their friends in the mix when they're meeting someone new," Tinder 's chief product officer, Mark Kantor, stated in a press release shared with Mashable. "Group Hangouts takes that even further, and we think it's going to be one of the most fun things we've ever built on Tinder. Step 2: Browse and match as a group Once a group has at least three members, it appears in other users' main Tinder stack (how people discover each other on the app). Your group can discover other groups, Like them, and match if it's mutual. Step 3: Take it offline Once your group matches with another, you can chat together and make IRL plans. Forty percent of Group Hangouts invitations were accepted in early tests in Australia. Once in a group, women were 2.2 times more likely to Like a group profile than a traditional profile. title: Tesla Roadster launch was postponed by two weeks due to high winds
body: Tesla 's second-generation Roadster could be the most postponed car ever. Originally announced in November 2017, and slated for a 2020 launch, the allegedly super-quick electric car has been delayed time and time again. After many, many teasers and subsequent delays over the last two years, Tesla was finally slated to unveil the Roadster on Oct. 1. Alas, that's not going to happen. On Monday, Tesla's official X account said the event has been rescheduled to Oct. 15. "We've been tracking the weather closely with local meteorologists, but given the severe conditions predicted because this event can only be held outdoors, we've made the difficult decision to reschedule. New date is October 15. Additional details to follow," the message said. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. Tesla CEO Elon Musk chimed in with a clarification of his own: "Due to high winds, the new Roadster demo is postponed by 2 weeks," he tweeted. The countdown timer on Tesla's website has now changed to reflect the Oct. 15 launch. SEE ALSO: Tesla launched Cybercab in Austin. Hours later, the feds launched an investigation. This, of course, caused a hurricane of tweets dunking on Musk saying, essentially, that windy weather shouldn't be a problem for a car. This is a car, however, that (according to Musk ) will be able to fly in certain configurations, at least over a short distance. It appears that the flying part will depend on the weather.

title: Cloudflare plans to issue quantum-safe TLS certificates
author: Dan Goodin
body: Cloudflare said Tuesday it plans to issue quantum-proof TLS certificates, making it one of the first authorities to issue such certificates that use a form of cryptography that is widely believed to withstand attacks from quantum computers. The Internet infrastructure provider said it will use an open source platform that issues both classic TLS certificates and a post-quantum equivalent known as Merkle Tree Certificates . The hybrid certificates will be free to both paying and non-paying users. To help build the massive system and establish ubiquity across the sprawling TLS ecosystem, Cloudflare will be acquiring an already trusted certificate root from CA GlobalSign. Cloudflare said the move will let millions of websites use post-quantum certificates at the flip of a switch and without incurring any increased performance overhead. Fundamental architectural changes ahead Cloudflare’s plans are part of a major overhaul in the web public key infrastructure (WebPKI) required to make website encryption and authentication safe for the coming post-quantum age. A major challenge is using quantum-proof signatures that can be easily transmitted during web requests and recorded in transparency logs to ensure counterfeit certificates aren't assigned to websites. The makeover will take years to complete, because it requires the work of an untold number of engineers who design operating systems, browsers, certificate authorities, and Internet infrastructure. title: Soon youll be able to get ready to pre-order the iPhone Duo
body: Apple 's first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo , will be available for pre-order on Oct. 16. But if you really want one, you can prepare for that moment four days in advance. Reddit users noticed that Apple's pre-order page for the iPhone Duo now says you can "come back on 10.12 to get ready for pre-order." To see what that means, just visit the pre-order page, where you can already pick your phone's finish and storage, choose whether you want to trade in an old device, and pick financing options, AppleCare coverage, and your preferred carrier. Right now, you can't really do much with that, as the "Continue" button is greyed out. But on Oct. 12, you'll presumably be able to save all that data, so you can pre-order the phone with one click when the time comes. The time will officially come at 5 a.m. PT (8 a.m. ET) on Oct. 16, and the iPhone Duo will start shipping to customers on Oct. 23. SEE ALSO: iPhone Duo wallpapers: How to download them now While there's no official word on this, rumors have long claimed that the iPhone Duo might be in short supply at launch . While not everyone will be able to pre-order it right away, making sure you have everything set up before the pre-order window opens might help you get your device a bit sooner. title: European spacecraft snaps stunning views of home and the moon
body: Europe's Jupiter-bound Juice spacecraft photographed Earth and the moon as it whipped past our home planet on Monday, stealing energy to fly the long trip. During its flyby, the European Space Agency's probe came within 5,370 miles of Earth, jetting over the Indian Ocean. It made its closest approach at 7:45 a.m. ET. One of its monitoring cameras captured Africa, and its navigation camera snapped Madagascar and the moon. Earth's gravity bent the spacecraft's trajectory by 20 degrees and sped it up by about 7,800 mph. Juice, short for Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer, burned little fuel to get that boost, officials said. The space flyby marked the mission's second Earth pop-in and ticked off yet another gravity assist to fling the spacecraft onward. The series of maneuvers began in 2024 with a combined moon-and-Earth flyby, and it also included a pass by Venus in 2025. Juice will return for a third and final Earth flyby in Jan. 2029, which should set it on its final course to Jupiter . It should arrive at the gas giant in 2031. "We used only a small amount of the propellant reserved for this flyby," said Angela Dietz, Juice's spacecraft operations manager, in a statement . "This gives us more to use at Jupiter to carry out observations of the planet's icy moons."
